::: {.eyebrow}
Start here
:::

This tutorial teaches **how to use PyCPT** to prepare, calibrate and evaluate
climate forecasts. The first case focuses on seasonal rainfall over Indonesia.
CPT is the calculation engine used by PyCPT when fitting models; operating or
building the standalone CPT application is not the subject of this tutorial.

## What you will learn

The first case follows CFSv2 rainfall forecasts over Indonesia. It introduces
CCA and PCR calibration, compares them with the raw model and climatology,
and examines how outcomes vary by season, location and training interval.
The notebook makes the calendars, common spatial support and scoring steps visible.

The [second case](../chapters/fit-diagnose-2023.qmd) opens the fitting workflow:
local X/Y/F inputs, actual CCA/PCR calls, model patterns and cross-validated
residuals for OND and JJA 2023. Its executed notebook requires the full fitting
environment when you run it; both cases can be read in a browser.

The [third case](../chapters/monthly-leads-2023.qmd) changes the question from
"how good is the forecast" to "how far ahead": one forecast issued on 1 November
2023, calibrated for each of the next six months, December to May. The
[fourth](../chapters/seasonal-leads-2023.qmd) does the same for the next six
three-month seasons and compares each season with its first month. The
[fifth](../chapters/dekad-leads-2023.qmd) moves to the subseasonal scale: every
October-December dekad, one to three dekads ahead, with GEFSv12. The
[sixth](../chapters/week-leads-2023.qmd) does the same by week, one to four weeks
ahead, at the native 0.05° grid of CHIRPS v3.0, and the
[seventh](../chapters/pentad-leads-2023.qmd) by CHIRPS pentad, one to six pentads ahead.

## Choose your path

| Your aim | Start here | What you need |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Learn to run PyCPT on your own forecast | [Learn PyCPT, chapter 1](../learn/01-first-case.ipynb) | A browser to read; the full PyCPT environment to run |
| Understand the findings | [Read the story](../chapters/indonesia-seasons-2023.qmd) | A browser; no PyCPT installation |
| Inspect how the results were produced | [Read the executed notebook](../notebooks/indonesia-seasons-2023.ipynb) | A browser; some familiarity with Python helps |
| Reproduce the figures and scores from saved results | [Offline analysis setup](reproduce.qmd#offline-analysis) | Scientific Python/Jupyter and the complete kit; no PyCPT or CPT installation |
| Fit the OND models through PyCPT | [Optional PyCPT refit](reproduce.qmd#optional-fit-ond-again) | Compatible PyCPT and its CPT engine, plus the supplied fitting inputs |
| Work through actual OND/JJA fitting and diagnostics | [Case-two story and notebook](../chapters/fit-diagnose-2023.qmd) | Browser to read; full PyCPT fitting environment to execute |
| See how skill changes with lead time | [Monthly](../chapters/monthly-leads-2023.qmd), [seasonal](../chapters/seasonal-leads-2023.qmd), [dekad](../chapters/dekad-leads-2023.qmd), [weekly](../chapters/week-leads-2023.qmd) and [pentad](../chapters/pentad-leads-2023.qmd) lead-time stories | Browser to read; full PyCPT environment and the CHIRPS v3.0 dekadal archive to execute |
| Examine assumptions and provenance | [Methods and limitations](methods.qmd) | The case question and its verification context |

::: {.callout-tip title="Reading and running are different activities"}
Reading either already-executed notebook needs only a browser. Running the first case's default
saved-results cells needs Python packages and the complete kit, but **no PyCPT,
CPT executable or IRI Data Library authentication**. Fitting new models through
PyCPT is an optional extension in case one and the central workflow in case two;
executing fitting cells requires the full PyCPT environment and compatible engine.
:::

## Mandatory, optional and helpful

| Status | Requirement | When it applies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mandatory | Browser | Reading the story or executed notebook |
| Mandatory for offline execution | Python, NumPy, pandas, xarray, Matplotlib, netCDF4 and Jupyter/IPython; the complete kit and a writable working folder | Recalculating figures and scores from saved results |
| Mandatory for model fitting | PyCPT with its compatible CPT executable | Case-two fitting notebook or the optional case-one OND refit |
| Conditional | Internet access, dataset permissions and authentication for protected data | Downloading new inputs; not needed for this packaged case |
| Optional | Quarto | Building the website locally; not needed to run the notebook |
| Helpful | Basic Python/Jupyter skills and familiarity with forecast seasons, calibration and verification | Following and adapting the code |

The [reproduction guide](reproduce.qmd) gives separate setup paths for offline
analysis and PyCPT fitting. Installing Python packages initially can require
internet access; "offline" refers to executing the saved-results workflow afterward.

## The story and notebook belong together

The **story** explains the question and findings in connected prose. Its controls
let you inspect metrics, seasons, training periods and province views. Hover or
tap a mark for details; focused charts also support keyboard navigation.

The **executed notebook** shows the code, calculations and static reference
figures. Read its outputs in the browser, or download the complete kit to run it.
The story and notebook present the same verified case results.

### Take a figure or a table with you

- **PNG** saves the complete current view, including its selected labels and legend.
- **SVG** is available for the six chart views, preserving vector marks and text.
- **CSV** follows the filter in an expanded data table.
- **NetCDF** provides the saved fields, scores and regional outputs through the [downloads section](reproduce.qmd#downloads).
- **Notebook reference PNG** opens the original executed figure. Its link label
  identifies its fixed metric or coverage, which can differ from your selections.

## Why PyCPT needs a CPT engine for fitting

PyCPT is the Python interface and workflow used in this tutorial. Its fitting
functions call the CPT executable to perform the calibration calculations.
The saved forecasts in this case were produced using **PyCPT 2.10.4, cptio 1.4.0
and CPT 17.8.3**. Those versions describe the tested fitting workflow, not a
requirement for browsing or running the offline analysis.

For the optional refit, use the supplied PyCPT environment specification, which
includes the compatible CPT engine. There is no need to compile CPT from source.
See the [tested fitting environment](reproduce.qmd#use-the-tested-debian-environment).
Upstream documentation describes [PyCPT's role](https://iri-pycpt.github.io/).

## When is IRI Data Library authentication needed?

No IRI Data Library key is needed to read this tutorial, execute case one's default
notebook or fit OND/JJA using the supplied local inputs. Authentication is needed
only if a workflow downloads a protected dataset that requires it. Do not infer
that requirement from the seasonal or subseasonal label alone: the
[official authentication guide](https://iri-pycpt.github.io/authentication/)
distinguishes public datasets from protected datasets and their access permissions.

## Read the calendar and the baseline first

Seasons are three-month windows. In the main case, their midpoint falls in 2023:
DJF starts in December 2022, while NDJ ends in January 2024. Adjacent windows
share months. They are not twelve independent annual verification samples.

The main training interval is 1991–2020; 1983–2010 is a sensitivity comparison.
Each calibration is compared with its matched climatology on the same evaluated
support. Read the [methods](methods.qmd) before interpreting a small difference
or generalizing beyond the case.
